1. Purpose, scope, governance and accountability
Purpose, governance and accountability

NDIA must operate an ICT Insider Threat and Risk Program under approved governance, with defined accountabilities for the Accountable Authority, CSO, CISO, security practitioners, system owners, HR, Legal, Privacy, Welfare, ICT and managers, covering employees, contractors and other users of NDIA systems.
NDIA must run an ICT Insider Threat and Risk Program with clear oversight, approved governance and named responsibilities for everyone who manages or uses NDIA ICT systems.
Governance requirement
Critical

2. Insider-threat risk management and control planning
Risk assessment, ownership and control planning

NDIA must assess insider-threat, fraud and corruption risks for ICT systems, data holdings, privileged roles and third-party access; assign accountable risk owners; define treatments and controls; and report risk and control effectiveness to governance forums.
NDIA must identify and assess insider, fraud and corruption risks for ICT systems and data, assign owners, choose controls and report how well those controls are working.

3. Security culture, conduct, training and acceptable use

NDIA personnel must understand and meet their security, confidentiality, integrity, acceptable-use and conflict-of-interest obligations, supported by induction, annual and role-based training and clear consequences for misuse.

NDIA must make sure everyone who uses NDIA ICT systems knows their security, privacy, confidentiality, acceptable-use and conflict-of-interest responsibilities and receives induction, annual and role-based training.

4. Confidential reporting, PID and reprisal protection
Reporting channels, PID handling and reprisal protection

NDIA must provide clear, confidential and protected channels for reporting insider concerns, including PID pathways, and must triage reports to authorised recipients while protecting identities and preventing reprisals.
NDIA must provide safe and confidential ways to report insider concerns, public interest disclosures, fraud and corruption, and must protect reporters from reprisal.

5. Personnel screening, clearances and suitability before access
Screening, clearances, waivers and temporary access

NDIA must complete identity, eligibility, suitability, work-right, security-clearance and waiver checks before granting access, and must only approve temporary or provisional access with documented risk assessment, approvals and supervision.
NDIA must confirm identity, work rights, suitability, screening and required security clearances before giving ICT access, and must tightly control any temporary or waiver-based access.

6. Access control, authentication and privileged access
Need-to-know access, MFA, privileged and remote access

NDIA must grant only approved, need-to-know access using unique identities, MFA, role-based authorisation and privileged-access controls, and must promptly review or remove access when roles, risk, location or employment status changes.

NDIA must give people only the ICT access they need for their role, use unique accounts and MFA, tightly control privileged and remote access, and remove or change access quickly when circumstances change.
